fish.name: Frostwhisker Dace
fish.flavor: Its whiskers freeze into tiny icicles that jingle when it panics. Local anglers call the sound 'the little bells of bad luck.'

fish.name: Mitten Minnow
fish.flavor: Covered in soft down that looks convincingly hand-knitted. Nobody knows who keeps losing exactly one of them.

fish.name: Button Sculpin
fish.flavor: Round, flat, and precisely the size of a coat button. Occasionally found sewn onto coats, still mildly annoyed about it.

fish.name: Snowmelt Guppy
fish.flavor: Born in spring puddles atop the ice, it spends its whole life convinced the lake is temporary. Technically, it's right.

fish.name: Chime Char
fish.flavor: Its ribs ring faintly when it swims through cold currents. A whole shoal sounds like a music box being apologized to.

fish.name: Woolly Smelt
fish.flavor: Grows a winter coat it never sheds. Sweats constantly, complains never.

fish.name: Porridge Loach
fish.flavor: Pale, lumpy, and warm to the touch for no reason science is comfortable with. Best caught before it cools.

fish.name: Candlefin Perch
fish.flavor: Its dorsal fin gives off just enough light to read by, provided you only read very short words.

fish.name: Shiverling
fish.flavor: It is not cold. It is just like this.

fish.name: Icicle Darter
fish.flavor: Hangs nose-down and perfectly still until something edible passes underneath. Then it remains perfectly still, but pointedly.

fish.name: Milkeye Chub
fish.flavor: Its clouded eyes see nothing at all, which it considers a mercy this far into winter.

fish.name: Grumble Trout
fish.flavor: Emits a low muttering audible through six feet of ice. Nobody has translated it, out of politeness.

fish.name: Teacup Flounder
fish.flavor: Curls up to fit perfectly inside a teacup, saucer sold separately. Offering it a splash of tea is considered good manners and better luck.

fish.name: Yawning Burbot
fish.flavor: Its mouth is stuck mid-yawn, which means either yawns are contagious across species or the lake is genuinely that boring. You yawn anyway.

fish.name: Knitfin Grayling
fish.flavor: Its fins grow in a flawless cable-knit pattern. The grandmothers along the lakeshore insist they taught it nothing.

fish.name: Hushfish
fish.flavor: Glides so quietly that the water forgets it was ever there. Anglers report catching one and only noticing hours later.

fish.name: Marrowglass Eel
fish.flavor: You can see clean through it to the fish it swallowed, who can see you, and would like a word.

fish.name: Winterkiss Koi
fish.flavor: Escaped from a temple pond three mountains away, or so it claims. Its scales stay exactly as warm as a held hand.

fish.name: Corkscrew Gar
fish.flavor: Its spiral snout drills fishing holes from below, for reasons of its own. Some anglers simply wait beside a likely spot and remember to say thank you.

fish.name: Snowblind Pike
fish.flavor: White as the ice it hides beneath, and just as patient. Mostly it ambushes prey; occasionally it ambushes itself.

fish.name: Kettlebelly Char
fish.flavor: Its belly stays stove-warm through the deepest cold. Old ice-fishers hold one for a while before letting it go, and neither party ever mentions it.

fish.name: Humming Bleak
fish.flavor: Hums a tune nobody remembers teaching it. If you hum along, it changes key and waits for you to catch up.

fish.name: Second-Moon Smelt
fish.flavor: Only rises when the moon's reflection freezes into the ice, then orbits the frozen copy like it owes it money.

fish.name: Mirrorkin Trout
fish.flavor: It swims exactly beneath your reflection, matching your every movement. Wave goodbye when you leave, or it will follow you home through the puddles.

fish.name: Selkie's Button
fish.flavor: A round silver fish said to be a button off a selkie's coat, still trying to swim back to its buttonhole. Return it to open water and something out there will owe you a favor.

fish.name: Frostwright's Apprentice
fish.flavor: It mends cracks in the glacier with careful mouthfuls of frost, one crystal at a time. It is not very good yet, hence the fishing holes.

fish.name: Yule Gulper
fish.flavor: Swallows anything wrapped, ribboned, or regretted. Catch one at midwinter and you may get back the year's worst gift, slightly improved.

fish.name: Hollow Choir Eel
fish.flavor: Its empty body echoes with the voices of every fish it once schooled with. On still nights the ice hums an old rounds-song in eleven parts.

fish.name: Ninth-Hour Grayling
fish.flavor: It only appears when the light can't decide whether it's day or night. Clocks near the fishing hole run slow out of respect.

fish.name: Grandmother Rime
fish.flavor: She remembers when the glacier was a river, and treats you accordingly. Being caught is a kindness she is extending, and she will want the hook back.

fish.name: Orrery Sturgeon
fish.flavor: The bony plates along its back are arranged in the constellations of a sky nobody has seen yet. Astronomers pay handsomely for a look; the sturgeon charges more.

fish.name: Sleepwalker's Lantern
fish.flavor: It carries a light that is not its own, sleep-swimming beneath the ice on an errand it never finishes. Wake it gently, or the light will go looking for a new carrier.

fish.name: The Auroral Shoal
fish.flavor: A single fish wearing the aurora as a school of a thousand. When it turns, the sky above the glacier turns with it, half a heartbeat late.

fish.name: Grandfather Below the Blue
fish.flavor: The old ones drilled offering holes and lowered down lanterns, songs, and their finest cheese. Something has kept this glacier quiet for a thousand years, and it has just noticed you.

fish.name: Winter's First Word
fish.flavor: Before the glacier, before the mountain, winter spoke a single word, and the word swam away before it could be taken back. When it passes beneath your ice hole, every snowflake for a hundred miles pauses to listen.
